reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the creator gives step-by-step instructions to join Forsage, including sending ETH, registering under a specified upline, and using the Forsage link provided in the description. The video actively facilitates paid participation in an upline-based structure rather than merely discussing or investigating it.

citations.quote: How to join Forsage ? How to deposit Ethereum in trust Wallet ? complete guideline...
Upline ID is 605690 this is the entry to apply for any job
By clicking on the register tool, it will be taken to the payment page
you will get the link of ForSag also in the description box just click that link

opening.argument: The video includes a concrete wallet-security caution rather than presenting participation as risk-free. Its on-screen warning says “12 Phrase keys Wallet info Don’t join without link,” and the narration explains that the recovery words are needed if the application is uninstalled or the phone is lost. The speaker therefore emphasizes protecting access credentials and using the correct link. Nothing in the supplied material promises profits, guaranteed returns, or effortless income. The payment discussion is procedural, while the security warning gives viewers a reason to verify the process before proceeding. On this record, the content is better understood as a cautious operational guide than deceptive financial solicitation.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats a wallet transfer and a registration page as proof of deceptive solicitation, but those elements establish only that the walkthrough involves a transaction. Its cited upline text does not state that viewers will earn commissions or receive guaranteed returns. Likewise, a link in a description can identify the destination for a tutorial. The supplied evidence shows procedural instructions and a wallet-safety warning, not a false earnings claim.

citations.quote: Upline ID is 605690 this is the entry to apply for any job
you will get the link of ForSag also in the description box just click that link

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The warning concerns recovering a Trust Wallet, not the risks of Forsage or losing money. It does not caution viewers against joining; instead, the narration directs them to deposit ETH, register, and approve payment. The absence of a stated profit guarantee does not remove the recruitment-dependent paid entry that the walkthrough actively enables.

opening.argument: The format and wording are instructional throughout. The creator says he will explain how to make a Trust Wallet account, then walks through selecting Ethereum, entering a recipient address, opening the dApps area, and locating Forsage’s registration page. He repeatedly describes what appears on screen and distinguishes joining from logging in. That is a technology and operational demonstration: it explains how a wallet and browser interface work. Showing where a payment page appears is not the same as certifying the external program or guaranteeing its outcome. The content can therefore be classified by its observable educational function rather than by assuming every demonstration of a registration process is an endorsement.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the video instructional does not make it a scam. The prosecution’s selected quotes show that the tutorial explains a process, but they do not show the speaker claiming personal success, promising income, or asserting that Forsage is safe. Even the phrase “apply for any job” is an unclear description in the transcript, not evidence of a commission structure. A demonstration may accurately show how to navigate a third-party interface without endorsing its claims.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: This is more than abstract education: the speaker tells viewers to open Forsage, choose “Join now,” register, and complete payment. The title calls it a “complete guideline,” and the narration says joining is easy. Those directions operationalize entry into the paid upline system, even without an explicit profit promise.

opening.argument: The available evidence shows ordinary cryptocurrency-wallet operations and a third-party registration workflow, but it does not establish the defining deceptive mechanism. The narration explains receiving ETH, copying a wallet address, entering an amount such as 0.1 ETH, and approving a transaction. The frames show a wallet with zero balances, send controls, and a Forsage page with join and login options. There is no supplied claim of guaranteed profit, no promised return, no stated downline income, and no request for the viewer’s recovery phrase. A paid registration or referral link alone does not prove fraud; it can be a service-access or referral process whose safety is not independently certified. The evidence supports ordinary operational promotion, not a demonstrated scam.

citations.quote: let's suppose, that i'm sending Ethereum amount 0.1 then i'll write 0.1 so it'll show the value of the total amount of dollars

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution infers a scam mechanism from payment plus an upline, but the cited material does not say that payment buys a guaranteed return or that recruitment produces income. The registration screen visibly presents both joining and logging in, which is consistent with access to an external service. A specified referral or upline can be an ordinary attribution feature; it is not, by itself, proof that the creator made a deceptive financial representation.

citations.quote: By clicking on the register tool, it will be taken to the payment page

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The missing guarantee is not the relevant gap: the evidence shows a paid entry placed under a named upline. The speaker tells viewers to register, approve the payment, and use the supplied Forsage link. That combination is a recruitment-dependent entry mechanism, not merely a neutral wallet demonstration. The zero wallet balance and lack of credential request do not change what the registration process requires.
